title: Invite balanced curiosity
principle: Offer one optional, light question about agreed common ground, then invite each person to take a turn.
scope: Short initial conversations and structured reciprocal disclosure.
limits: Immediate liking is not lasting friendship or attraction. Question-asking paper has a 2025 correction retaining conclusions: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40111841/.
promptGuidance: Make the invitation optional. Share a little yourself; leave room to answer or skip.

title: Respond to what someone chooses to share
principle: Suggest a relevant follow-up and listening with care instead of an interrogation script.
scope: Question-asking, perceived responsiveness, and immediate liking in dyadic conversations.
limits: Measured responsiveness does not establish every causal mechanism. No inference about emotion, personality, or relationship health is licensed.
promptGuidance: Ask a follow-up only if welcome; do not presume how the other person feels.

title: Describe common ground accurately
principle: Use mutually declared interests or values as conversation starting points.
scope: Meta-analysis of actual and perceived similarity across interaction stages.
limits: Actual similarity's association weakens beyond initial contexts; perceived similarity may reflect attraction. Shared labels do not calibrate a pair's fit.
promptGuidance: Say 'you both selected this interest'; let the owners decide whether it matters.
prohibitedUses: Turning soft interests into hard requirements

title: Offer a bounded collaboration experiment
principle: For collaboration intent, offer a small optional activity with a concrete purpose and a clear stopping point.
scope: A proposed introduction format inspired by professional network opportunities.
limits: The source tests job mobility on LinkedIn, not this activity, partner reliability, or collaboration quality. This proposal needs direct evaluation.
promptGuidance: Use an agreed interest and purpose. Invite a brief idea exchange before any commitment.

title: Offer opportunities without predicting chemistry
principle: Describe an eligible introduction as a possible opportunity; let real interaction and owner choice determine whether it continues.
scope: Pre-meeting romantic prediction limits; acquaintance well-being associations; professional opportunities.
limits: Two speed-dating studies do not establish universal impossibility. Acquaintance findings are associative; job effects vary by tie definition and industry. None validates Kin.
promptGuidance: Allow a low-pressure hello. State ranking as a deterministic ordering, never a probability of romance, happiness, or success.

title: Keep human consent in control
principle: Both owners choose disclosure and continuation. Skipping, declining, withdrawing, or blocking must remain valid outcomes.
scope: Kin's consent and data-minimization policy; cited studies provide context, not validation of this architecture.
limits: This is an ethical design commitment, not an empirical claim that consent controls alone prevent harm.
promptGuidance: Use only validated, mutually disclosed facts. Remind owners they can skip any prompt and decide independently.
prohibitedUses: Sharing raw private history without explicit disclosure consent
